name: F-4 Overseas Korean visa

requirement_groups.name: Korean ancestry, any nationality (unified since 12 Feb 2026)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires that the applicant, or a parent or grandparent, once held Korean nationality (including those who left before the government's establishment) and subsequently acquired a foreign nationality. Since 12 Feb 2026, this single standard applies equally regardless of the applicant's country of origin -- previously, overseas Koreans from China and 6 former Soviet states faced additional income, education, or work-experience screening before qualifying for F-4, and were routed into the separate, now-discontinued H-2 status if they didn't meet it.
requirements.fix_path: Document Korean-nationality ancestry via family registry, discharge certificate, or birth/marriage certificates linking the applicant to a former Korean-national parent or grandparent.

requirements.blocker_text: Cannot be issued to someone who currently holds Korean citizenship or Korean permanent residence in a way that would make F-4 redundant.

Men who left Korea or first lost Korean nationality on or after 1 May 2018 are restricted from F-4 status until 31 December of the year they turn 40, unless they have completed or been exempted from Korean military service.
requirements.fix_path: Complete or obtain exemption from Korean military service, or wait until the applicable age threshold.

requirements.blocker_text: As part of the 2026 H-2/F-4 unification, applicants must complete a 5-hour early-adaptation program (crime prevention and safety orientation) in the initial settlement stage, and are barred from F-4 status if they have a criminal history involving murder, rape, drug offences, or voice-phishing fraud.
requirements.fix_path: Complete the mandatory early-adaptation program and confirm no disqualifying criminal history.

evidence_required.document: Family relationship certificate, discharge certificate, family register, or birth/marriage certificate proving Korean-nationality ancestry
Proof of foreign nationality acquisition (own or ancestor's, where applicable)
Criminal record certificate from country of residence and any country of 6+ months' residence

outcome.duration_length: up to 3 years (up to 1 year without Level 1 Social Integration Program completion, up to 3 with it, per multiple sources)

sources.title: Ministry of Justice Notice No. 2026-35 (법무부 고시 제2026-35호, 재외동포(F-4) 취업활동 제한범위 고시), published via HiKorea, governing F-4 employment-activity restrictions under the unified overseas-Korean status effective 12 Feb 2026
KOWORK Visa Center -- F-4 Overseas Korean visa guide, corroborating the male military-service age restriction (born/left after 1 May 2018, restricted until age 40)
KOWORK -- H-2/F-4 integration policy summary, effective 12 Feb 2026, describing the 5-hour early-adaptation program and criminal-history bar

notes: STRUCTURAL FINDING, and the single most significant live event caught in the Korea build: effective 12 February 2026, Korea unified its two-tier overseas-Korean status system -- previously, ethnic Koreans from China and 6 former-Soviet-bloc countries (the largest overseas-Korean populations) faced extra income/education/work-experience screening for F-4 and were routed into the separate, more restrictive H-2 (Working Visit) status if they didn't qualify, while overseas Koreans from other countries faced no such extra screening. As of the unification date, the Ministry of Justice stopped issuing new H-2 visas entirely, and F-4 eligibility now applies identically regardless of country of origin -- see kr_h2_working_visit_closed for the corresponding closed-route file marking this transition formally. Several English-language guides checked in this research pass, including some dated after the merger, still describe H-2 and F-4 as two separate, currently-issuable statuses -- a direct live-staleness catch matching this dataset's core thesis, arguably the clearest and most consequential example found in the Korea build given the scale of the population affected (H-2 quota had reached roughly 303,000 at its peak before shrinking to about 80,000 by mid-2025 as F-4 conversions absorbed most of the demand). citizenship_after_months (24) and pr_after_months (24) reflect the fast simplified track available to overseas Koreans generally -- among the more favourable ancestry-to-citizenship timelines in this dataset, though not as fast as Poland's Karta Polaka (12 months) or instant repatriation (0 months); Korea's route requires an actual residence period even for confirmed ancestry, unlike Poland's ancestry routes. dual_citizenship_allowed is false, consistent with Korea's general single-nationality rule for naturalisation, though F-4 holders retain their existing foreign nationality indefinitely while on F-4 status itself -- the false value here refers specifically to the eventual naturalisation step, not to holding F-4 status.
